content:
Julie (Support): FYI -> Acme reported a large spike in incorrect facts from our hosted endpoint after last night's rollout. They say replies now invent dates and cite non-existent docs. Escalating, customer is pretty upset. Request id examples: req_0a1b2c3d, req_0f9e8d7c
Alex W: thanks, Julie. Can you paste the customer prompt + one of the regression responses? Also which model variant rolled?
Julie (Support): Model: redwood-instruct-1.3 (traffic switched 2026-03-15 02:11 UTC). Repro prompt below (sanitized):
```
System: You are a concise assistant.
User: Summarize the release notes for Acme Payment v2.3 and include migration steps.
```
Customer reported output (wrong): "The migration requires editing /etc/acme-config which does not exist. Also run `acme-migrate --legacy`"
Expected output (previous baseline): No mention of /etc/acme-config, migration uses admin console export/import steps.
Maria D: hmm, initial hypothesis: the new tokenizer/formatting change in rollout might have changed system message handling. We switched the default system prompt sanitization on for this model variant. Could cause hallucination if instruction parsing altered.
Sanjay R: also check that we didn't accidentally route requests to a different persona variant. I saw a canary that had extra "creative" persona enabled during rollout.
Eve (QA): I pulled logs for req_0a1b2c3d:
```
{"req": "req_0a1b2c3d", "model": "redwood-instruct-1.3", "variant": "v1.3-canary-creative", "latency_ms": 210, "trace_id": "trace-77ab"}
```
Eve (QA): That variant is the problem. The canary was supposed to be isolated, but the routing policy allowed 5% traffic and the canary tag leaked to the hosted pool due to a tagging bug.
oncall-bot: @channel Incident priority: P1 - customer-facing output regression (affecting >=1 paying customer)
Alex W: OK immediate steps: 1) Roll back routing to force 100% traffic back to redwood-instruct-1.2-stable. 2) Start a hotfix to revert the persona change for the canary. 3) Notify the customer and open incident postmortem. Who can push the rollback now?
deploy-bot: Initiating rollback job: rollback-job-1761234578 queued.
Maria D: I'll run the routing rollback. Command: `rwdctl routing apply --target redwood-instruct-1.2-stable --scope hosted --force`
Sanjay R: I'll prepare a quick config patch to disable the creative persona in the canary and mark it quarantined:
```
patch: disable_persona: creative
canary: traffic: 0
```
Eve (QA): Repro steps for others: send the exact customer prompt to /v1/chat with model redwood-instruct-1.3 and variant v1.3-canary-creative, include conversation history. I can repro locally and get same hallucination.
Julie (Support): I've sent a brief update to Acme: "We see a regression after a canary change. We're rolling back routing now and will follow up with mitigation steps and a root cause." They want ETA on fix.
Alex W: Maria, once rollback command finishes, post confirmation here with the active model backend IDs and a couple sample responses to verify. Also ask Acme for fresh failing req ids if they have them.
Maria D: rollback done at 1761234670. Active backend: redwood-instruct-1.2-stable -> instances (stb-07, stb-11). Verified 100% traffic on stable.
Maria D: sample response after rollback to stable for the same prompt: "To migrate to Acme Payment v2.3, export settings from admin console, use the migration guide steps A->B, and test in staging. Do not modify system files." (looks correct)
Sanjay R: patch applied to quarantine canary variant and disabled persona flag. Marked tag `quarantine/1761234685`.
deploy-bot: Hotfix deploys: patch-deploy-1761234689 succeeded. Canary variant traffic set to 0%.
Eve (QA): Run a quick 50-sample sweep for the prompt family against stable vs canary to confirm quality delta. I'm seeing stable accuracy 96% vs canary 61% for factuality checks.
Alex W: Good. Julie, please tell Acme we've rolled back to the previous model, provided ID, and are running a QA sweep. Offer to re-run any earlier jobs and request any more failing examples.
Julie (Support): Message sent. They asked if we will rollback for everyone or patch the canary. I told them we'll keep stable for now and quarantine the canary until patching and extra validation. They want a follow-up in 2 hours.
Maria D: Action items: - postmortem ticket (infra: routing bug) - patch code review to fix tagging. I'll open the PR and link here. - add automated canary isolation checks, gate if persona flags differ from stable.
Sanjay R: I'll add a regression test to CI that rejects persona drift and run a model-signature compare on rollout.
Eve (QA): I'll attach the QA sweep logs and sample diffs to the incident.
Alex W: After QA, we'll consider rolling forward with corrected persona settings, but only after a closed canary with 0 drift. For now, P1 mitigated.
oncall-bot: Incident status changed to: mitigated (customer rollback applied).
Julie (Support): Acme acknowledged and is satisfied for now. I'll keep monitoring and will reopen if they see more. Thanks team :thumbsup:
Alex W: Save all artifacts (req ids, model bundles, deploy logs) under INC-1761234567. We'll run a short RCA tomorrow.
Eve (QA): Filed artifacts at https://confluence.redwood/INC-1761234567 and added sample diffs.
Alex W: closing thread for now, keep me posted if Acme reports anything else.
